cross_cutting.content:
Sendbird's AI concierge service 'delight.ai' (Image provided by Sendbird)

As the adoption of AI by companies expands, the way customers are interacted is also changing. Marketing departments utilize AI agents for product rec...

As the adoption of AI by companies expands, the way customers are interacted is also changing. Marketing departments utilize AI agents for product recommendations, sales for lead management, and customer support for handling inquiries. However, if these different systems cannot share customer information, customers will have to repeat the same explanations even after the introduction of AI. To address the issue where internal departmental divisions persist in AI services, Sendbird has introduced an integrated AI agent that connects all customer touchpoints into a single system.

Sendbird (CEO Kim Dong-shin) announced the launch of 'Delight Customer Agent,' which handles everything from shopping and reservations to customer support and retention, and 'Midas,' an AI agent management tool, under its brand AI concierge service 'delight.ai.'

The two products unveiled this time target different problems that arise in the process of companies utilizing AI. While Delight Customer Agent integrates customer service tasks scattered across departments and channels, Midas supports field personnel in managing agents' work methods and operational policies without the help of developers.

While AI agents are rapidly spreading within enterprises, connectivity between systems remains a challenge. According to Salesforce's 2026 survey, 50% of AI agents operated by companies run independently without being connected to other agents. Furthermore, the rate of interconnected applications within the enterprise was only 27%. This implies that even if the level of automation for individual tasks is increased, the service experience can be disjointed if the customer purchasing, consultation, and after-sales support processes are not interconnected.

To address these issues, Sendbird developed an integrated agent that handles various tasks centered on customer relationships. The Delight Customer Agent provides four functions: shopping, reservations, customer support, and customer retention. It is designed so that a single agent handles everything from supporting product browsing and purchasing to order changes, exchanges and refunds, and contract and membership renewals.

The key feature is the ability to maintain the context of the conversation with the customer. Agents remember customer preferences and past purchase and consultation history, and can utilize previous conversation content across different channels, such as chat, voice, and email. For instance, if a customer inquires about delivery status or the refund process after purchasing a product based on an AI recommendation, the consultation continues based on information gathered during the purchase process. The focus is on reducing the inconvenience of customers having to explain their order details or purchase purpose from scratch.

It supports not only product recommendations based on customer purchase history and preferences but also the screening of potential customers and scheduling of consultations. It also includes features to provide relevant information at the time of contract or membership renewal and to offer appropriate benefits to customers at risk of churn. These tasks are designed to be performed in accordance with policies, permissions, and approval procedures pre-established by the company.

#### Revising AI Work Guidelines via Natural Language… 'Midas', a Field-Centric Operations Tool

Midas, launched alongside it, is a product focused on transforming the way AI agents are built and operated. Once companies adopt AI agents, they must modify their systems whenever customer response policies, promotions, or business processes change. Previously, these changes were often requested from the development organization, making it difficult to immediately reflect the needs of the business units. Midas supports business personnel by enabling them to directly configure and improve the agent's workflow by inputting necessary details using natural language.

The main functions consist of four categories: implementation, testing, analysis, and improvement. When a manager writes customer response guidelines or operational policies in natural language, the AI agent converts them into business processes that can be executed. Before applying to an actual service, the system can be tested with virtual customers to verify expected responses and processing steps.

During operation, business procedures can be modified to reflect new policies or promotions, and customer conversations and operational results are analyzed to suggest areas for improvement and follow-up actions. Sendbird believes that through this, companies can reduce their dependence on development organizations when changing AI agent response methods or business processing procedures, and adjust services to meet customer needs.

"Every company wants its AI agents to perform more tasks and improve performance, but until now, even small changes required development work," said Nick Singh, Head of Product at Delight AI. "With Midas, frontline personnel can apply necessary changes within hours without waiting for support from the development organization. This will enable the continuous enhancement of AI agent capabilities and performance."

Kim Dong-shin, CEO of Sendbird, emphasized, “There is a risk that the disconnect between existing organizational departments will be repeated in the AI environment as companies adopt AI. Customers do not care which department handles shopping, customer support, or repurchase. Just as they form a relationship with a single brand, AI must also be able to consistently understand and maintain the relationship and context with the customer.”

The product unveiled by Sendbird is an attempt to expand the scope of customer service automation while extending the operational authority of AI agents to the field.

If product recommendations, consultations, and after-sales support are connected based on a single set of customer information and conversational context, companies can manage overall customer relationships beyond simply automating individual tasks. However, in actual operating environments, integration with each company's existing systems, customer data management, and task approval frameworks are expected to determine the level of service utilization.

It is expected that the extent to which Delight Customer Agent and Midas can improve customer response efficiency and service quality while meeting these conditions will determine their competitiveness in the future market.

# Delight.ai Launches Delight Customer Agent and Midas

Delight Customer Agent unifies the customer journey, while Midas gives business teams a new way to build, test and improve the agent using natural language.

#### Topics

Delight.ai, Sendbird’s portfolio of customer agents for enterprises, has introduced Delight Customer Agent, one AI agent designed to handle shopping, booking, support and retention, and Midas, a self-service AI agent management tool that lets teams build, test, and continuously improve their Delight Customer Agent using conversations.

These two new product introductions symbolise the next phase of the company’s focus on expanding what AI can do to create better customer experiences and help businesses grow, without forcing them to rely on a patchwork of separate tools.

For decades, companies have raced to deploy AI chatbots to handle customer-facing interactions, but this has led every department to build or buy its own AI agent.

New research from Gartner shows that just 4% of customer service organisations have achieved the ROI they expected from AI initiatives, and Gartner predicts that by 2028, organisations that build AI portfolios will achieve twice the business value of those pursuing standalone AI use cases*.

Instead of giving marketing, sales, customer support and other teams separate AI agents that only understand one piece of the customer lifecycle, Delight Customer Agent is one agent that sits across the entire customer lifecycle so businesses can easily maintain customer context across all interactions and channels, making it easier for brands to help customers discover a product, complete a purchase, resolve a support issue and return for their next purchase without forcing them to start over.

“Brands are at risk of recreating the same organisational silos with AI that have frustrated customers for decades,” said John Kim, Co-Founder and CEO of Delight.ai.

“Customers do not care which department owns shopping, support or retention. They have one relationship with a business and expect AI to understand their relationship.”

One Agent for Every Department

Delight Customer Agent is built on a different model: one agent for every customer-facing job. It brings four critical functions together in the same foundation: Shopping, Booking, Support and Retention.

Delight Customer Agent understands the customer’s identity, preferences and history, reaches customers across channels and can take actions all while operating within the company’s boundaries, approvals and oversight.

With Delight Customer Agent, businesses can:

- Shop: guide product discovery and purchases;
- Book: qualify leads and book meetings, appointments and jobs;
- Support: resolve issues and questions; and,
- Retain: renew, re-engage, and grow customer relationships and lifetime value.

“Whether a member is browsing for a grill, looking up club hours, or asking about a renewal, they’re talking to the same agent,” said Scott Vandegrift, VP of product at BJ’s Wholesale Club.

Delight Customer Agent is Easy For Anyone to Use

In addition to Customer Agent, Delight is introducing Midas, an AI agent that enables any team within any department to build and continuously improve their Delight Customer Agent without relying on engineering or IT to implement requests.

Instead of waiting for updates to be made, Midas gives teams closest to the customer a self-service way to manage their Delight Customer Agent.

Teams can now easily describe what they want the Delight Customer Agent to do in natural language, and Midas will translate that request into an actionable process for the agent to follow.

Midas works across four stages:

- Build: turns workflows and policies into a process the Delight Customer Agent can follow;
- Test: runs proposed changes against simulated customers so teams can see how the agent responds before a real customer does;
- Improve: implements approved updates, including new policies, offers and requests; and
- Analyse: reviews conversations and results to identify where the Delight Customer Agent falls short and recommends what teams should improve next.

“Every team has a running list of things they want their AI agent to do better, but today, every change becomes an engineering problem,” said Nick Singh, Head of Product at Delight.ai.

“Midas changes that, and instead of waiting days for an update, those closest to the customer can make necessary changes in hours and can keep making updates so the same agent becomes smarter and more capable over time.”

#### About the Author

Sophia Bennett is a news curator at Martechvibe, covering global developments across marketing technology, digital transformation, AI, data, and customer experience trends.

Sendbird于10日宣布，在旗下品牌AI礼宾服务delight.ai上推出AI代理“Delight Customer Agent”，并同步发布基于自然语言的AI代理管理工具“Midas”。两款新产品将购物、预约、客服及复购留存等环节打通，进一步拓展企业在客户服务场景中的AI应用。

Delight Customer Agent是一套整合购物、预约、客服和客户留存四大核心能力的AI解决方案。过去由不同部门分别承接的客户服务环节，如今可由同一AI代理统一处理，覆盖从商品浏览、下单购买到售后支持，以及复购和留存运营等多个阶段。

Sendbird CEO Kim Dongsin表示，企业在引入AI时，原本存在的部门割裂问题也可能被复制到AI体系中。对客户而言，他们并不会区分购物、客服和复购分别由哪个部门负责；既然客户与品牌之间的关系是连续的，AI也应当能够基于统一的客户关系与上下文持续提供服务。

# FPT proposes 5 pillars for co-creating AI and quantum computing.

At the recent Vietnam-Japan Public-Private Forum on Economic and Scientific-Technological Cooperation in Tokyo, FPT proposed five pillars of co-creation in AI, quantum computing, human resources, and technology finance, and also signed memoranda of cooperation with Japanese partners on unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and the low-altitude economy.

Speaking at the forum, FPT Chairman Truong Gia Binh noted that AI is driving science, technology, and innovation at an unprecedented pace, and this is an opportunity for Japan and Vietnam to complement each other's strengths and create value that surpasses the capabilities of each side. From this, FPT proposed five pillars of cooperation between Vietnam and Japan.

First, we need to build a sovereign, reliable AI infrastructure, connecting AI factories, data, and application capabilities of both countries on the principle that each side owns its own infrastructure and data. Next, we need to transform businesses and supply chains with AI in the automotive, electronics, logistics, and energy sectors. Following that, we need to train tens of thousands of AI and quantum engineers on a large scale, proficient in Japanese. Fourth, we need to establish a Vietnam- Japan Co-creation Fund. Fifth, we need to promote cooperation in the quantum era.

According to Mr. Truong Gia Binh, these five proposals need to be implemented on the basis of close cooperation between the governments of the two countries, universities, and leading technology companies in Vietnam and Japan. "We are not only cooperating for mutual development, but also jointly creating a new future for both nations," he said.

At the event, FPT and its Japanese partners exchanged Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs). In the low-income economy sector, the Vietnam Low-income Economic Alliance (LAEP), led by FPT, signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Kaga National Strategic Special Zone Promotion Association. The two sides aim to promote the low-income economy in Vietnam and Japan, explore the formation of industrial clusters and related production facilities in Kaga City, and jointly leverage data and AI to develop new business models.

With the MoU between FPT and NTT e-Drone Technology, a leading UAV company in Japan, the two sides plan to collaborate on developing remote controllers for drones, surveying the UAV market in Vietnam, implementing pilot projects (PoC), and expanding distribution channels...

cross_cutting.description: South Korean AI chip developer Rebellions and SK Telecom have announced a collaboration to build sovereign AI infrastructure in Korea ... Deployment targeted for 2028 The collaboration is part of South Korea’s broader effort to build domestic AI capabilities spanning chips, infrastructure and services. The ministry said it
cross_cutting.content:
Nvidia, South Korean AI chip developer Rebellions and SK Telecom have announced a collaboration to build sovereign AI infrastructure in Korea, connecting locally designed neural processing units with Nvidia’s rack-scale platform and SK Telecom’s data centers, models and services.

The November 9 agreement, supported by Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT, gives the country a concrete path for deploying domestic AI accelerators alongside Nvidia infrastructure. It also links the planned systems to SK Telecom’s public-facing services, including work under Korea’s AI for All program.

Connecting Korean NPUs to Nvidia infrastructure

Rebellions plans to use Nvidia NVLink Fusion to connect its next-generation Rebel R200 neural processing units within racks. The company will also use Nvidia’s MGX rack architecture and reference designs while developing the systems.

NVLink Fusion is designed to let custom processors connect to Nvidia’s scale-up networking and infrastructure ecosystem. Under the planned architecture, Nvidia GPUs would handle the prefill stage of AI inference, while Rebellions NPUs would perform the decode stage. The companies said this division could improve throughput and power efficiency, although they did not disclose benchmark results or a testing schedule.

Rebellions is developing the R200 for low-latency inference on frontier models. The company said its chip will support large mixture-of-experts models, but the announcement did not provide final specifications, pricing or manufacturing details.

SK Telecom plans to deploy the systems in its AI data center and connect them with its proprietary foundation models, including A.X K2. Its role covers data center operations, models and public services, while Nvidia supplies interconnect and rack-platform technology and Rebellions contributes the locally designed accelerator.

Deployment targeted for 2028

The collaboration is part of South Korea’s broader effort to build domestic AI capabilities spanning chips, infrastructure and services. The ministry said it will support cooperation between Nvidia and Korean NPU companies, beginning with Rebellions and SK Telecom, and also work with Nvidia on physical AI and GPU supply.

Rebellions’ R200 systems are expected to be ready for deployment in 2028. SK Telecom said it intends to connect the resulting infrastructure with its models and services as part of its full-stack sovereign AI strategy.

# SoftBank and Grab Plan US$1.85B AI Infrastructure Investment in Malaysia

Funding will flow in stages as projects hit development and customer milestones, with the partners targeting five gigawatts or more across Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia.

Free Newsletter

Get the hottest Fintech Malaysia News once a month in your Inbox

SoftBank Group and Grab have signed joint development agreements with Petroleum Sarawak Berhad (PETROS) to develop AI infrastructure in Malaysia.

The companies have proposed US$1.85 billion in initial combined seed capital as the first stage of a multi-year build-out targeting five gigawatts or more of AI compute capacity across Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia.

SoftBank will contribute US$1 billion, Grab US$750 million and PETROS US$100 million.

The investment will be deployed in stages as projects reach key development and customer contract milestones and meet the necessary closing conditions.

The companies will seek additional investors and hyperscaler customers as the projects expand.

Once fully operational, SoftBank, Grab and PETROS will use the facilities to serve governments, multinational companies and small businesses across the region.

#### How SoftBank and Grab are splitting the two projects

SoftBank, Grab and PETROS will jointly develop the Sarawak project, building on a framework agreement they signed in Kuching on 8 October.

The project has a proposed initial investment of US$1 billion, comprising US$800 million from SoftBank and US$100 million each from Grab and PETROS.

Grab has an option to increase its stake in the Sarawak project. Exercising the option would reduce SoftBank’s stake, although SoftBank would remain the majority shareholder.

Grab will lead the Peninsular Malaysia project as its founding shareholder, contributing US$650 million of the proposed US$850 million initial seed capital.

SoftBank will provide the remaining US$200 million. Grab also plans to bring in long-term strategic investors as the project scales.

The project will rely on third-party equity and non-recourse project financing to fund further development.

“AI infrastructure will power the next wave of growth, and Malaysia has the talent and ambition to help lead it. Together with Grab, we will build the capacity needed to support Malaysia’s digital ambitions and accelerate AI innovation across Southeast Asia,”

said Masayoshi Son, Chairman and CEO of SoftBank Group Corp.

“Together with SoftBank Group, we plan to build critical AI infrastructure in Malaysia, where Grab began, for all of Southeast Asia. This infrastructure will allow us to accelerate the development of localized AI solutions for our communities,”

said Anthony Tan, Co-founder, Chairman and CEO of Grab.

#### AI usage in Southeast Asia could grow 60-fold by 2030

The companies cited the e-Conomy SEA 2026 report by Google, Temasek and Bain & Company, which estimates that per capita AI usage across Southeast Asia’s six largest economies is currently around one-tenth of the level in the US.

The report projects that regional AI usage could grow by up to 60 times by 2030.

The projects will be developed in collaboration with Malaysia’s Federal Government and the Sarawak Government.

The projects will support the National AI Action Plan 2026–2030 (AI Nation 2030). They will also align with Sarawak’s Post COVID-19 Development Strategy 2030.

The companies said the facilities will follow Malaysia’s renewable energy use guidelines. They will also feature high-efficiency infrastructure to reduce water consumption and reliance on local power grids.

#### Governance and the SoftBank lock-up

Anthony Tan will oversee the development of both projects and appoint dedicated management teams to handle day-to-day operations while continuing to lead Grab. Grab’s board has reviewed and approved his affiliation with the projects.

SoftBank has agreed in principle to a five-year lock-up on Grab shares held directly by an entity within SoftBank Group, subject to customary exceptions.

Beyond AI infrastructure, the companies will also explore other areas of mutual interest in Malaysia, including advanced manufacturing.

The initiatives will create high-value jobs in engineering, design and technical fields while advancing Malaysia’s technology development goals.

# SoftBank Group and Grab sign joint development agreements to develop AI infrastructure in Malaysia

###### Via SoftBank Group

Nov 10, 2026

- SoftBank Group and Grab, together with PETROS, announce plans for US$1.85 billion in initial combined seed capital to build AI infrastructure across Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia
- Projects to be developed in partnership with global investors and hyperscalers, with a long-term target of five gigawatts or more of AI compute capacity, and a vision to move up the AI ecosystem over time
- Initiative supports Malaysia's AI Nation 2030 ambition and strengthens Malaysia's position as a regional AI hub

SoftBank Group Corp. (TSE: 9984, “SBG”, and together with its subsidiaries and affiliates, the “SoftBank Group”) and Grab Holdings Limited (NASDAQ: GRAB) (“Grab”) today announced the signing of joint development agreements in connection with plans for US$1.85 billion in initial combined seed capital, together with Petroleum Sarawak Berhad (“PETROS”) to develop AI infrastructure in Malaysia.

The collaboration aims to establish AI infrastructure in Malaysia to meet the growing demand for computing capacity across Southeast Asia and globally. Once fully operational, the facilities are expected to be amongst the largest AI infrastructure of their kind in Asia, providing governments, multinational companies and small businesses with reliable access to advanced computing capabilities.

The combined investment forms part of a multi-year plan to develop AI compute capacity across Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia, with a long-term target of five gigawatts or more. The proposed initial combined seed capital is US$1.85 billion, comprising US$1 billion from SoftBank Group, US$750 million from Grab and US$100 million from PETROS.

The proposed investment will be deployed in stages subject to projects achieving key development and customer contract milestones, and the necessary closing conditions. The parties will also seek additional investors and hyperscaler customers to support project development and expansion.

“AI infrastructure will power the next wave of growth, and Malaysia has the talent and ambition to help lead it. Together with Grab, we will build the capacity needed to support Malaysia’s digital ambitions and accelerate AI innovation across Southeast Asia,” said Masayoshi Son, Chairman and CEO of SoftBank Group Corp.

“Grab’s mission is and always has been, the technological advancement and economic development of Southeast Asia. Southeast Asia is one of the world's fastest-growing digital economies, and Grab is at the forefront of developing AI solutions for the region. Together with SoftBank Group, we plan to build critical AI infrastructure in Malaysia, where Grab began, for all of Southeast Asia. This infrastructure will allow us to accelerate the development of localized AI solutions for our communities. Through this partnership, we can drive faster regional AI development and adoption, bringing its transformative benefits to many millions of people, while contributing to Malaysia's economy through the creation of high-value jobs and AI upskilling,” said Anthony Tan, co-founder, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Grab.

## POWERING SOUTHEAST ASIA'S AI-DRIVEN FUTURE

Research by Google, Temasek and Bain & Company indicates that per capita AI usage across Southeast Asia's six largest economies is currently around one-tenth of the level in the United States, with regional AI usage projected to scale by up to 60-fold by 2030*. Meeting this anticipated demand will require substantial investment in AI infrastructure within the region.

The projects will be developed in close collaboration with Malaysia's Federal Government and the Sarawak Government, aligning with the National AI Action Plan 2026–2030 (AI Nation 2030) to position Malaysia as an inclusive and sustainable AI nation, as well as Sarawak's long-term development aspiration under the Post COVID-19 Development Strategy 2030. The facilities will operate in line with Malaysia’s renewable energy use guidelines, and feature high-efficiency infrastructure designed to reduce water use and reliance on local power grids.

Beyond AI infrastructure development, the parties will explore other areas of mutual interest, including advanced manufacturing in Malaysia. These initiatives are expected to create high-value employment opportunities in engineering, design and technical fields, while supporting the objectives of the National Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) Policy and the Malaysia Digital Economy Blueprint (MDEB). They will also help accelerate advanced technology adoption, improve productivity and strengthen the capabilities of Malaysia's workforce.

## PROJECT OVERVIEW AND INVESTMENT

The Sarawak project will be jointly developed by SoftBank Group, Grab and PETROS, building on the Framework Agreement signed in Kuching on October 8, 2026. The proposed initial investment in the Sarawak project is US$1 billion, comprising US$800 million from SoftBank Group, US$100 million from Grab and US$100 million from PETROS. Grab has an option to increase its stake, which will cause SoftBank Group’s stake to decrease, albeit with SoftBank Group remaining as the majority shareholder. Further details are set out in the announcement issued by the three parties on November 9, 2026.

The proposed initial seed capital for the Peninsular Malaysia project is US$850 million, comprising US$650 million from Grab and US$200 million from SoftBank Group. As the project’s founding shareholder, Grab will lead its development and bring in long-term strategic investors as the project scales, diversifying its funding base. Further development is expected to be funded at the project level through third-party equity and non-recourse project financing.

Anthony Tan is expected to oversee the development of both projects and appoint dedicated management teams to run day-to-day operations while continuing to lead Grab and create value for Grab and its ecosystem partners. The Grab Board has reviewed and approved his affiliation with the projects.

Given the parties' mutual interest in developing the AI ecosystem in Malaysia, SoftBank Group has agreed in principle to a five-year lock-up in respect of Grab shares that will be held directly by an entity within SoftBank Group, with the lock-up to take effect in accordance with the agreed terms and subject to customary exceptions.

* Google, Temasek and Bain & Company, e-Conomy SEA 2026: report

## About SoftBank Group Corp.

The SoftBank Group invests in breakthrough technology to improve the quality of life for people around the world. The SoftBank Group is comprised of SoftBank Group Corp. (TSE: 9984), an investment holding company that includes stakes in AI, smart robotics, IoT, telecommunications, internet services, and clean energy technology providers, as well as a majority stake in Arm, which is building the future of computing; and the SoftBank Vision Funds, which are investing to help transform industries and shape new ones. To learn more, please visit https://group.softbank/en.
